ops.title: 2026-07-07 stale-widget incident — cask upgrades never recycle a live WidgetKit appex (frozen render); fixed v0.45.1 daemon reap keyed on binary ctime vs process start
ops.body:
2026-07-07: the Notification Center widget froze at "stale · 1h ago" while the TUI was fresh. Root cause: a `brew upgrade` of the cc-pool-status cask replaces `/Applications/CCPoolStatus.app` on disk, but WidgetKit/chronod NEVER recycles a live `CCPoolStatusWidget.appex` process — the leftover (deleted-binary) instance wedges the reload pipeline, and the host app's `reloadAllTimelines()` pokes render nothing. The widget's aging "stale · Nh ago" footer is its honest pre-rendered timeline tail doing its job. Unwedge = `kill -9 <appex pid>`; chronod respawns the on-disk binary within seconds.

Fixed in cc-pool v0.45.1 (`daemon/widgetheal.go`): every poll, the daemon reaps widget appexes whose start time predates the on-disk binary's **ctime** beyond 5s slack, reconfirmed on (pid, StartedAt) before SIGKILL; `ccp doctor` reports the condition advisorily.

Platform facts proven live:
- **ctime vs mtime**: a cask's ditto copy preserves mtime (= build time) but ctime = install time. Staleness must key on ctime; mtime gives false negatives on rebuilds.
- **KERN_PROCARGS2's exec path** (first NUL-terminated string after argc) is kernel-captured at exec(2), survives binary replacement/unlink, and for chronod-spawned appexes is byte-identical to the plain bundle path (no translocation) — safe for string-equality matching (`procscan.ProcsByExecutable`).
- **Daemon-package tests** neutralize the reap seams in `holder_test.go` TestMain (like `reapOrphanedServers`): `widgetBinaryPath` → absent path, `killPID` → no-op. Without that, pollOnce tests scan real processes and could SIGKILL a real appex on a post-upgrade machine.

Secondary unexplained observation (ccn doc 0b7923c): the wedged pre-upgrade appex burned ~15 CPU-min in ~1h (bursty, idle under sampling); no spin-capable widget code — attributed to chronod re-render churn. Watch for recurrence on a current binary.

Related: [[fp-backend-rollout]] (group-container consent re-prompts every upgrade — separate upgrade hazard), [[orphan-nfsv4-reaping]] (the kill-time reconfirm pattern this reap mirrors).
